overview: A one-page State Department file index for decimal file 894.56, concerning the training and mobilization of Japanese merchant-marine personnel. It records a Yokohama report on training practices, the circulation of that report to the Treasury, Commerce Department, and U.S. Maritime Commission, and those agencies’ favorable assessments of its quality. It also notes Beppo R. Johansen’s authorship of the report and cross-references a Moscow telegram from Harriman quoting a Tokyo despatch on extraordinary measures and the mobilization of seamen in Japan.

subfiles.title: Index sheet for reports on Japanese merchant-marine personnel

subfiles.about: The sheet indexes correspondence concerning the training and mobilization of Japanese merchant-marine personnel.
subfiles.summary: The index lists a Yokohama report associated with Boyce and prepared by Beppo R. Johansen on the training of Japanese merchant-marine personnel. It records the report’s circulation to the Treasury Department, Commerce Department, and U.S. Maritime Commission, all of which judged it excellent, adequate, or satisfactory. A final entry cross-references Harriman’s March 20 telegram no. 947 from Moscow, which quoted a Tokyo despatch titled “Extraordinary Measures in Japan” concerning the mobilization of seamen and its publication in Moscow newspapers on March 19.

interest: The sheet is useful for reconstructing a larger documentary chain even though the underlying reports and letters are not present here. It identifies the otherwise obscured author of the Yokohama report, documents unusually enthusiastic evaluations by three U.S. government bodies, and links routine merchant-marine training intelligence to wider concern about Japanese mobilization measures. The Moscow cross-reference also shows how American diplomats monitored Soviet press publication of information originating in Tokyo.
